title: Jimmy Jackson's band, the union, and the Eureka brass band
summary: After Rena he played with Jackson's band (later the Gibson band), explains his lack of work in the 1930s and the union dispute after his breakdown, then describes the Eureka's trumpet section and personnel.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Well, what happened after you left René? Well, that's when I tried to organize my own band. I didn't have any luck. Oh, I see. So, uh, let me see now. Then after that, who did you join up with? Well, it was quite a while. They had a man by the name of Jimmy Jackson. Jackson had a band. And he got in touch with me whenever he'd get parade jobs, well he'd hire me, play with them. Jackson's band, Jimmy Jackson's band. And what did he play? He didn't play anything at all. He was mostly a music director. He'd walk in front of the band with his stick. Remember who was in that band? I can remember. They had a trumpet player. They had Dave Bailey playing drum. Batiste Brown was one of the trumpet players. Now the rest of the musicians, I've just lost memory of them. Is this the band that later became the Gibson band? I think it is. Jackson's band was turned over the Gibson band. That's the band I'm playing with now. E. Gibson's band. And so then after that, let's see, you played with Jackson, was that during the Depression or after? That was after Depression. After Depression, after 1929. That's right. And was it before World War II? It was after World War II. Well how long did you play with Rene? Well Rene, I played with Rene in about a year and a half. That was the first band I started playing with. First time I started playing music. And Perez wasn't as much as it is now. Well who did you work with during the 30s and during World War II? In World War II? No. No. Music wasn't doing much then. I don't think I was playing anybody then. And during the 30s you weren't playing with? No. No. Things was dead then. You didn't get in the WPA band or anything like that? No I didn't get in on that WPA band. I see. So after World War II you joined up with Jackson's band? Yeah. And how long did you stay with Jackson's band? Well I wasn't exactly a steady musician with Jackson. Just whenever he'd be short of a trumpet player he'd use me. I was just an extra there. Don't you have a paper from the union showing when you joined up? Didn't you show me that Sunday? Yeah. Yes I do. Well we could tell from that when you joined the union. I wish I had a... You don't have that with you now? I don't have that with me. If I'd have known this I certainly could have brought it. Well we'll see it later. Yeah. So you don't know about when it was you joined the union? No, no. When I joined the union I was playing with Rene, Kid Rene's band. That's a long time ago. That's right. That's right. Tats' daddy signed that paper you have from the union. It was Tats' daddy, old man Alexander. I think it was. I'm not sure. Yeah that's right. I remember that from Sunday. So after you left Jimmy Jackson who did you go with? Well after I left Jimmy Jackson I wasn't playing any, music was slow then, I wasn't doing much. Now the next band I started playing with was the Eureka. I played with the Eureka quite a while. I guess I overwake myself. I was pressing, I had my own pressing shop, and trying to play music too. Well that caused me to have a nervous breakdown. And I didn't have an idea I'd get strong enough to play music. I had to give all that up, playing music again. And well that's how I did to get out of the union. I was playing with the Eureka when I had that nervous breakdown, not one of those dudes showed up to see anything. What had happened to me? And when I did get up to start back to playing music, my intention was to go back into the union. But I was told he wouldn't permit me that policy. So that's why I had him join back in the union. So he wouldn't give you insurance? He wouldn't give me an insurance policy. All that time I had paid them, had been in there. Well when you were with Jackson, were you in the union? Jackson, no. I don't remember if I paid any union dues when I was with Jackson. Must not have been. I don't remember. I don't think that was a union band. I'm trying to remember. I think it ever was. Plenty how you joined up the Eureka, who were the trumpets in? In the Eureka? Mm-hmm. Poisa Humphrey was one, and T-Boy. T-Boy was the other trumpet player. They had three. Poisa Humphrey, T-Boy and myself. T-Boy and Ramey? Yeah, that's right. He left and went away. And then I think that's when Pagio came in. Well how did that trumpet section work? Who would play the lead when Ramey was there? Well Poisa Humphrey would play the lead. And Ramey would play the second. And I would play second and sometime lead. I didn't have any third parts. Well how would you line up? Who would be on the right? Poisa Humphrey would be on the right. I'd be in the middle. And T-Boy would be on the left side. Well why do they line the trumpets up that way? Who is the middle man? Well your middle man mostly is your second. On your right is your first. And in the middle is your second. Well sometime you get a man to play third but very seldom you get trumpet arranged to that. So it would be two lead men in one second. The second trumpet would be in the middle? Yeah. Well what is the second trumpet part like? What does he play? Well it's mostly, he mostly plays in the staff or under the staff. The second part very seldom would go over the staff. Well does the second trumpet play carry the melody or does he play a harmony part or what? I don't understand. It's mostly a harmony. Or if he has a lead, it's right under the first trumpet part. It's arranged below the first trumpet. And he can hold a lead like that. He'd carry the lead and the other guy would play it up higher the same thing, an octave up. Yeah, that's right. Your second is just an octave lower. Who else was in the Eureka then? Trombones? Well Albert Warner and Sonny Henry, that was the two trombone players. And then as I told you the drummer was, Son was playing drums with him. Son Fuclos. Yeah, he played snare drums. Now I'm trying to think of the bass drummer. I can't call his name. Son Fuclos was a bass drummer. Son was a bass drummer. Not a snare drummer. I can't remember his name. Was he in the band before Arthur Ogle? Hogan you know? No, I don't remember Arthur Ogle. You don't remember him? No. Arthur Ogle and Arthur Ogle. He was a drummer? Mm-hmm, he's a snare drummer. Turn the machine off a second. I don't remember him. I don't remember him. Well, you used to play with him. Yeah. But he was with him for years there. And he lost his legs. He just kind of lost his legs. They had Son White and Ernest Rogers in there too for a while, after him. Yeah. But anyway. I did remember Son White. Mm-hmm. Let's see, when you first came into the Eureka, who was playing tuba? Clok. This man they called Clok. His name is Clok. Red Clok. Yeah, they mostly know him by Red. Did they have baritone horns and pec horns then? No. Or did they have saxophones? No. They had Roddy on sax and Manuel Paul. Two sax. And let me see, who are we missing here? Who haven't we got? Did they have a clarinet ever? Well, sometimes they would use George Lewis. But they mostly used a sax. It's a Roddy and Manuel Paul was a sax player. Very seldom used the clarinet. So as time went on, let's see, who changed in there? Fair little change. Well, this other trumpet player that was playing with Poison Amphrey and myself, I'll call his name just now. Remy, yeah. Well then he left. He went away. And Paggio came in. And that's how things went on. Yeah, I guess they've had too many changes other than that while you were with him. No. Other than Paggio. Things didn't change. No, they didn't. Who was the trumpet player before you were with him? Whose place did you take? I don't, they didn't have, I can't remember any other. You don't remember whose place you took? No, I don't. I know Landry and Schatz were in there for a while. Both of them. Because when I went in there they had T-Boy and Poison Amphrey. Let me see now. So you went in the Eureka. And what did they play? What kind of jobs did they have? Well they mostly played parades. That's all I ever played with them was parades. They have a band for that occasion. Well they had to do something else. They had funerals too. Well that's what I mean. I never did play a dance like with them. Mostly we played with parades. Well they used parades for funerals and these different organizations it turns
